resources.string: Chinese chess
Chinese chess (xiangqi). Tap one of your red pieces, then a green dot to move it. The marks on each piece show how it moves. Trap the black general so that it cannot escape.
Your turn: tap one of your red pieces
Tap a green dot to move there
Check! Your general is attacked: protect it
Pieces
How the pieces move

Pieces stand on the line crossings. On each piece, a dot is one step that way, two dots are two steps, an arrow means any distance, an arrow with a bar means it jumps over one piece to capture, and a hollow dot is allowed only after crossing the river.
General (帥, 將): one step along a line, always inside the palace. The two generals may never face each other on an open line.
Advisor (仕, 士): one step diagonally, inside the palace only.
Elephant (相, 象): two points diagonally, never across the river. Blocked if the point in between is taken.
Horse (馬): one point straight, then one diagonally outward. Blocked if the first point is taken.
Chariot (車): any distance along a line, like the rook in chess.
Cannon (炮, 砲): moves like the chariot, but captures only by jumping over exactly one piece.
Soldier (兵, 卒): one step forward. Once across the river it may also step sideways. It never goes back.
Checkmate!
No legal move left: in Chinese chess that loses the game.
Draw: the same position came back three times.
Draw: 60 moves each without a capture.
Draw: neither side has a piece left that can attack.
